o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish باغلو (baġlu). By surface analysis, bağ + -lı.
Morphologically from qorx- + -u. Cognate with Turkish korku.
From Proto-Turkic *kadgu (“sorrow”). Cognate with Turkish kaygı, Uzbek qaygʻu, Chuvash хуйхӑ (hujh̬ă, “grief, sorrow”), Bashkir ҡайғы (qayğı) (see more there).
Borrowed from Russian абажур (abažur), borrowed from French abat-jour, from abat (“breaks down”) + jour (“light”).

Present participle compound of uzaq (“far”) + vurmaq (“to strike”).
Calque of Russian дальнобо́йный (dalʹnobójnyj).
From Arabic عِيَال (ʕiyāl) through Persian عیال. Compare Uyghur ئايال (ayal), Uzbek ayol, Turkmen aýal.
From Proto-Common Turkic *koč (“ram”). The secondary sense 'strong/brave man' is mostly present in Oghuz languages and adjacent varieties.
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish قوشلق (quşluq), from Proto-Oghuz قُشْلُقْ (qušluq). By surface analysis, quş + -luq. Compare Turkish and Gagauz kuşluk, Turkmen guşluk, Salar goşluq.
